lens: Code-shape independent of stated goal — type misnomers, approximate-when-exact-feasible, panics/unwraps in lib code, silent data drops, fake-enforcement-named-as-real
answer: v4+v5 carry six type-misnomers (projected_tokens_p95 acts as a constant when n<10; UsageWindowSnapshot doc says 'audit-only' but its projected_tokens_p95 field is read for enforcement at §B.4 step 13.5; InboxStore::dead_letter trait-doc claims 'atomic' but trait-level prose cannot enforce file-system atomicity without a WAL/journal pattern; SettingsRenderer::render trait-doc claims 'Atomic: tempfile + rename(2)' without qualifying same-filesystem; ProviderFamilyKey contradicts its own rationale by deriving Ord on a wrapper of an enum the plan asserts lacks Ord; the SessionTicket invariant fence Send+Sync+'static admits Arc<T> and therefore does NOT enforce the documented 'no Arc' value-only claim), one explicit unwrap-in-library-code (v4 §B.4 step 5: accounts.iter().find(|a| a.id == exp.chosen_account_id).unwrap()), and three silent-drop classes (drifting-account exclusion in v5 AccountSnapshotProvider returns the same RouteError::NoEligibleAccount as 'zero-accounts-configured'; saturating_add on tokens_out hides overflow under a hard cost ceiling; '?'-placeholder in stop_hook_supported survives because C.12.bis only greps autonomy_tier). Two of these — the unwrap and the enforcement-via-audit-field on UsageWindowSnapshot — are CRITICAL F5 violations that the v5 delta did not introduce but the consensus debate must surface because they remain in the v4-as-foundation that v5 composes onto.
key_claims: v4 §B.4 step 5 contains a literal `.unwrap()` in supervisor-app library code: `let acc = accounts.iter().find(|a| a.id == exp.chosen_account_id).unwrap();` — if `RoutePolicy::select` returns an account_id stale-vs-snapshot (race between snapshot read and select), this panics at runtime in the daemon's hot loop. F5 unwrap-in-library-code violation.

v4 §B.2.1 `UsageWindowSnapshot` doc says 'Audit-only. Live UsageWindow remains the enforcement+reconciliation source of truth' but v4 §B.4 step 13.5 reads `snap.projected_tokens_p95` and calls `inbox.dead_letter` on the basis of that read — the field IS used for enforcement; the 'audit-only' claim is a type-misnomer / silent-enforcement-via-audit-field anti-pattern.

v4 §B.6 + grit unit tied to `projected_tokens_p95` says 'When n<10: projected_tokens_p95 = cost_ceiling_tokens (conservative seed)' — feeding that into v4 §B.4 step 13.5 `if snap.projected_tokens_p95 > ticket.cost_ceiling_tokens` evaluates to `if cost_ceiling > cost_ceiling` which is ALWAYS false, so the enforcement is a no-op for every cold-start (provider, model_hint) pair; the name 'projected_tokens_p95' is a misnomer when the underlying value is a constant equal to the ceiling itself.

v4 patch #6 makes `InboxStore::dead_letter` 'atomic' via trait doc-comment ('Atomic lock-release + dead-letter transition. dead_letter MUST only be called on a currently-locked message; the call consumes the lock'). Trait-level prose cannot enforce file-system atomicity. The JsonlInbox impl on POSIX has no native atomic primitive across two file operations (release-lock + write-dead-letter-row); a naive impl that calls release then write would silently break the contract under SIGKILL between the two — fake-enforcement-named-as-real.

v4 §B.2.1 invariant fence `fn _f<T: Send + Sync + 'static>() {} _f::<SessionTicket>();` claims to enforce the value-only / no-Arc rule from §A.1 P3, but `Arc<T>` is itself `Send + Sync + 'static`. The fence does not detect Arc fields; it only detects Rc/RefCell/non-static borrows. The 'no Arc' guarantee is therefore enforced only by human field-level inspection at acceptance C.2 — not by the cited invariant fence.

v5 §B.2.1 `ProviderFamilyKey(pub ProviderFamily)` carries `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd)]` but the rationale comment states 'ProviderFamily is Copy but not Ord by derive; explicit key type'. For the wrapper's derive to compile, the inner enum MUST itself implement Ord/PartialOrd — contradicting the rationale. Either the rationale is false (then the wrapper is dead weight) or the derive cannot compile (impossible derivation). type-misnomer / contradiction-with-stated-fact.

v5 §B.2.2 `SettingsRenderer::render` doc says 'Atomic: tempfile + rename(2). Idempotent.' rename(2) is atomic only when source and destination share a filesystem; cross-FS rename falls back to copy+unlink, which is NOT atomic. The doc is unqualified. If `$CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR/settings-drift/<id>` and the rendered target path land on different filesystems (CI runners with separate /tmp mounts), the 'atomic' guarantee silently degrades. fake-enforcement-named-as-real.

v5 §B.4 `AccountSnapshotProvider::snapshot()` extension semantics: 'If VerifyMode::FailOnDrift and any account's DriftReport.entries contains a non-Match state, the account is excluded from the returned Vec<ProviderAccount>.' Exclusion is silent — the supervisor's tick_once step 4 calls `RoutePolicy::select` on a possibly-empty list and gets back `RouteError::NoEligibleAccount`, losing the actual cause ('account X excluded due to drift'). The drift outcome only surfaces in `.omc/state/settings-drift-report.json` side-channel, not in the supervisor's own error path. silent-data-drop.

v5 §B.4 `VerifyMode::AutoReconcile` calls `SettingsRenderer::render` and 'then includes it in the snapshot' — the doc is silent on what happens if `render` returns `SettingsRendererError`. If the implementation ignores the error and includes the still-drifting account, drift persists silently while the snapshot reports success. silent-data-drop.

v4 §B.4 step 7.5 uses `saturating_add` on `projected.tokens_out`: overflow silently caps at u64::MAX. For a cost-ceiling check that wants to fail-fast when projected exceeds budget, saturating arithmetic hides the overflow case (when actual usage would have been astronomically larger than represented). `checked_add` returning `Err(SupervisorError::UsageBlocked('overflow'))` is exact and feasible. silent-data-drop / approximate-when-exact-feasible.

v4 §B.5 capability seed has `stop_hook_supported = ?` and `request_id_supported = true/false`. C.12.bis (B.11 row 12) enforces only `grep -c '^autonomy_tier = "T[1-4]"' == 3`. There is NO acceptance check for `stop_hook_supported = ?` placeholder survival. If conformance build.rs fails to fill `stop_hook_supported`, the `?` survives into runtime and downstream code either parse-errors or defaults silently. silent-data-drop.

v4 §B.4 step 9 `WindowExpired => self.rotate_window(); recurse once` — the lock acquired in step 1 is held during recursion. v4 patch #6 'Early-return lock-release rule' covers ERRORS but not RECURSION; if `rotate_window()` returns Ok the recursion fires holding the prior lock, and a second `inbox.peek_lock` may attempt to acquire on top of an existing one. The 'recurse once' bound is informal — no lock-stack discipline declared.

v5 §B.2.2 `verify` uses `content_blake3` byte-hash for drift detection. A JSON file edited by an outside tool that reorders keys (e.g. running `jq` to pretty-print) is byte-different but logically Match — drift will report Modified for a no-op edit. Structural diff (parse-then-compare-AST) is exact and feasible for JSON/TOML at the byte cost of a parse. approximate-when-exact-feasible.

v5 §B.3 ProviderOverrides for Codex declares `omitted_hook_events = []` ('Codex DOES support hooks — verified ~/.codex/hooks.json 9.2K'). The HookEventMap (kernel HookEvent → Codex event name) is not yet captured (R1 fixture is gated on Wave-4d scaffold-time `cp ~/.codex/hooks.json crates/.../tests/fixtures/codex-hooks.observed.json`). Until the fixture lands, the empty `omitted_hook_events` ASSUMES every kernel HookEvent variant has a Codex equivalent — a 10-variant assumption with zero evidence. approximate-when-exact-feasible (gate the empty list on fixture existence).

v5 §B.3 hook command template `$WORKSPACE_ROOT/tools/foundry-supervisor-stop-hook` uses string placeholder substitution. Renderer must implement the substitution. Plain `str::replace` is approximate (collides with literal `$WORKSPACE_ROOT` in user content; allows half-substituted prefixes like `$WORKSPACE_ROOT_OVERRIDE`). A typed `EnvVarRef::Workspace | EnvVarRef::Home | EnvVarRef::Custom(String)` enum collected from a build-time scan of allowed roots is exact. approximate-when-exact-feasible.

v5 C.30 acceptance row claims hooks_supported per-driver enforcement via `grep -c 'hooks_supported' registry/capabilities/foundry-supervisor.toml >= 3`. The grep counts occurrences of the literal word, not value validity — `hooks_supported = banana` would pass. fake-enforcement-named-as-real (the count gate is necessary but does not validate the value).
type_misnomers_detected: UsageWindowSnapshot.projected_tokens_p95 — named 'p95' but degrades to constant `cost_ceiling_tokens` when n<10 (v4 §B.6); under cold-start, the field equals the ceiling and the §B.4 step 13.5 enforcement check `projected_tokens_p95 > cost_ceiling_tokens` is always false → naming a no-op 'projected p95'

UsageWindowSnapshot — doc says 'Audit-only. Live UsageWindow remains the enforcement+reconciliation source of truth' but the snapshot's projected_tokens_p95 field IS read for enforcement at v4 §B.4 step 13.5 (gates inbox.dead_letter)

InboxStore::dead_letter trait doc-comment says 'Atomic lock-release + dead-letter transition' — trait prose cannot enforce file-system atomicity; only the impl can (and the JsonlInbox impl on POSIX has no native primitive without a WAL/journal)
SettingsRenderer::render doc says 'Atomic: tempfile + rename(2)' — rename(2) is atomic only on same-filesystem POSIX; cross-FS falls back to copy+unlink (non-atomic); doc is unqualified

ProviderFamilyKey derives Ord/PartialOrd while the rationale comment claims 'ProviderFamily is Copy but not Ord by derive' — wrapper derive REQUIRES inner derive; the rationale and the derive are mutually exclusive (one is wrong)

SessionTicket invariant fence `_f::<T: Send + Sync + 'static>()` is documented as enforcing the 'value-only / no Arc' invariant (§A.1 P3) but Arc<T> satisfies Send+Sync+'static; the fence does not detect Arc fields

TickOutcome::Saturated — variant name and §B.4 saturation note both correctly say `try_acquire` returns immediately and no lock is held; this is NOT a misnomer (verified against §B.4 in-text). Recorded here as a watch-list item that resolved cleanly.
approximate_vs_exact_findings: projected_tokens_p95 rolling p95 over n=100 samples — by definition admits 5% breach; for hard cost-ceiling enforcement, exact rolling-max or hard-cap is feasible and more honest
content_blake3 byte-hash for drift detection — flags semantically-identical JSON/TOML with reordered keys as Modified; structural parse-then-compare is exact and feasible at parse cost
saturating_add on projected.tokens_out (v4 §B.4 step 7.5) — silently caps at u64::MAX; checked_add returning Err(UsageBlocked('overflow')) is exact and feasible

100ms-cadence file-existence poll for stop_hook_path (v4 §B.3) — inotify (Linux) and kqueue (macOS) provide event-driven exact detection; chosen approximation acceptable but trade-off never named in plan

ProviderOverrides for Codex declares omitted_hook_events=[] without the R1 fixture in place — assumes all 10 kernel HookEvent variants map to Codex with zero evidence; gating the empty list on fixture existence is exact and feasible
Hook command $WORKSPACE_ROOT placeholder substitution — string-replace is approximate (collides with literal occurrences, allows half-substituted prefixes); typed EnvVarRef enum is exact
C.30 grep -c 'hooks_supported' >= 3 — counts presence of the literal word, not value validity; toml-parse + per-row enum-membership check is exact
panic_unwrap_locations: v4 §B.4 step 5 (supervisor-app library code, in tick_once): `let acc = accounts.iter().find(|a| a.id == exp.chosen_account_id).unwrap();` — explicit `.unwrap()` in the daemon's hot loop. If RoutePolicy::select returns a stale account_id (race between snapshot read and select), this panics. CRITICAL F5 violation. Fix: `.ok_or(SupervisorError::NoEligibleAccount)?`

v4 §B.4 step 9 `WindowExpired => self.rotate_window(); recurse once` — `rotate_window` failure path not declared; if it panics the lock acquired at step 1 leaks. Speculative panic-on-recursive-failure-path.
silent_drop_locations: v5 §B.4 AccountSnapshotProvider::snapshot() with VerifyMode::FailOnDrift — drifting accounts are EXCLUDED from the returned Vec; downstream RoutePolicy::select then returns RouteError::NoEligibleAccount, which is indistinguishable from 'zero accounts configured'. Drift outcome surfaces only in the side-channel `.omc/state/settings-drift-report.json` — the supervisor's own error path drops the cause silently

v5 §B.4 VerifyMode::AutoReconcile — calls SettingsRenderer::render and 'includes the account in the snapshot'; doc is silent on what happens if render returns Err. If error is swallowed, drift persists silently while snapshot reports success

v4 §B.4 step 7.5 — saturating_add on projected.tokens_out hides u64 overflow under a hard cost ceiling; the check passes when the true projected value would have exceeded the ceiling by orders of magnitude

v4 §B.5 capability seed `stop_hook_supported = ?` placeholder — C.12.bis only enforces `autonomy_tier` does not contain `T?`; a `?` in stop_hook_supported survives the build → downstream code parse-errors or defaults silently

v4 §B.4 step 9 `WindowExpired => self.rotate_window(); recurse once` — 'recurse once' bound is informal; if the window keeps expiring (clock skew, infinite expiry), the recursion is unbounded and the lock acquired at step 1 is never released across recursion levels

v5 §B.4 trait-doc says drift outcomes are written to `.omc/state/settings-drift-report.json` 'for the CI lane to consume' — at supervisor RUNTIME (not CI), nobody reads this file; runtime exclusions disappear from observable supervisor state
uncertainty_areas: Whether the v4 §B.4 step 5 `.unwrap()` is intentional shorthand in the plan that the executor will lower to `.ok_or(...)?` at scaffold time, or whether it is the literal contract — plan does not say either way

Whether the JsonlInbox impl of `dead_letter` is expected to use a WAL/journal pattern to honor the trait's atomic contract, or whether the contract is best-effort — v4 patch #6 declares the contract but does not specify the implementation strategy

Whether `projected_tokens_p95` is a true rolling p95 from a sorted window or a streaming approximation (t-digest, P²-algorithm) — v4 §B.6 says 'rolling p95 of last 100 (provider, model_hint) samples' but the algorithm is not named; either could be valid, but the test in row 33g cannot distinguish

Whether the `mtime`-based idempotency assertion in v5 C.28 actually exercises the no-write path — if `render` always tempfile+renames, mtime updates regardless of content equality and the test would force the impl to pre-check content hash; this is an indirect test for an unstated implementation requirement

Whether v5 §B.2.1 ProviderFamilyKey actually compiles given the rationale — F5 cannot verify without invoking rustc; if the inner enum needs a separate Ord derive added at account-kernel:23-29, that is an existing-kernel surface change that should trigger lean-a10
Whether VerifyMode::AutoReconcile error swallowing is real or speculative — v5 §B.4 prose simply does not say; this is a doc gap, not an observed bug

findings.summary: Explicit `.unwrap()` in supervisor-app tick_once hot loop on accounts.iter().find(...) — panics on stale account_id race
UsageWindowSnapshot documented 'audit-only' but its projected_tokens_p95 field gates inbox.dead_letter at step 13.5 — enforcement-via-audit-field
Trait doc claims 'Atomic lock-release + dead-letter transition' — trait prose cannot enforce file-system atomicity; JsonlInbox impl needs WAL/journal pattern (unspecified)
Send+Sync+'static fence claimed to enforce 'no Arc' invariant; Arc<T> satisfies the bound — fence does not detect Arc fields
Drifting accounts silently excluded from snapshot; cause disappears into RouteError::NoEligibleAccount, surfacing only in `.omc/state/settings-drift-report.json` side-channel

When n<10, projected_tokens_p95 = cost_ceiling_tokens makes step 13.5 check `cost_ceiling > cost_ceiling` always false — cost-ceiling enforcement is no-op for every cold-start (provider, model_hint) pair
Wrapper derives Ord while rationale claims inner enum lacks Ord — derive requires inner Ord; rationale and code contradict, one is wrong
'Atomic: tempfile + rename(2)' unqualified — only true same-filesystem POSIX; cross-FS rename falls back to copy+unlink (non-atomic)
Byte-hash drift flags reordered-but-equivalent JSON/TOML as Modified; structural diff is exact
saturating_add on projected.tokens_out hides u64 overflow under a hard cost ceiling; checked_add is exact
stop_hook_supported = ? placeholder is not enforced by C.12.bis (only autonomy_tier is greped); ? survives into runtime
Counts literal word presence, not value validity; `hooks_supported = banana` would pass C.30
'recurse once' is informal; rotate_window failure path holds the step-1 lock across recursion; unbounded retry possible if the window keeps expiring
render() error path not specified — if error is swallowed, drift persists while snapshot reports success
Hot poll vs inotify/kqueue event-driven detection; chosen approximation acceptable but trade-off never named
String-replace approximate (collisions, half-substitutions); typed EnvVarRef enum is exact

findings.anchor: v5 §B.3 Codex omitted_hook_events=[] before R1 fixture
findings.summary: Empty omitted_hook_events ASSUMES all 10 kernel HookEvent variants map to Codex; gating the empty list on fixture existence is exact

fixuptasks: F5-FIX-UNWRAP-IN-TICK-ONCE-1: Replace `.unwrap()` at v4 §B.4 step 5 with `.ok_or(SupervisorError::NoEligibleAccount)?`; add a unit test that exercises the stale-account_id race (snapshot returns Vec without exp.chosen_account_id) and asserts Err(NoEligibleAccount), not panic

F5-FIX-USAGEWINDOWSNAPSHOT-RENAME-OR-RELOCATE-1: Either (a) rename UsageWindowSnapshot.projected_tokens_p95 to make its enforcement role explicit and drop the 'audit-only' doc, OR (b) move projected_tokens_p95 off the snapshot into a dedicated `EnforcementProjection` value that is plumbed separately into step 13.5; keep snapshot truly audit-only

F5-FIX-INBOXSTORE-DEAD-LETTER-IMPL-CONTRACT-1: Add an ADR fragment specifying the JsonlInbox dead_letter implementation strategy (WAL line-write-then-fsync-then-state-flip OR rename-based journal); add a crash-injection test (extension of v4 row 5) that SIGKILLs between the lock-release and dead-letter-row write and asserts the post-recovery state is exactly DeadLettered (not Released, not Locked)

F5-FIX-SESSIONTICKET-NO-ARC-PROCEDURAL-CHECK-1: Replace the Send+Sync+'static fence claim with a real check — either a build.rs scan that greps the SessionTicket-bearing module for `Arc<` / `Rc<` / `Box<dyn` substrings on declared field types, OR a documented constraint that any future field addition requires a fence test that fails on Arc<u8> compile-time

F5-FIX-PROVIDERFAMILYKEY-RECONCILE-1: Either add Ord/PartialOrd derive to ProviderFamily at account-kernel:23-29 and delete ProviderFamilyKey (lean-a10 ceremony required), OR replace ProviderFamilyKey's derive with a manual Ord impl on a discriminant-int and update the rationale comment to say 'ProviderFamily Ord deferred to v6 to keep account-kernel public-API surface frozen'

F5-FIX-SETTINGSRENDERER-ATOMIC-QUALIFY-1: Amend SettingsRenderer::render doc to qualify atomicity as 'atomic on same-filesystem POSIX rename(2); cross-FS not supported, render returns SettingsRendererError::Io if temp-dir and target-path are not on the same device' AND add a renderer init check that asserts (or rejects) cross-FS configurations

F5-FIX-ACCOUNTSNAPSHOT-DRIFT-ERROR-CHANNEL-1: Promote drift-induced exclusion from a side-channel JSON file to an explicit SupervisorError variant (e.g. `SupervisorError::AccountExcludedByDrift { account_id, drift_paths }`) returned through tick_once when no other accounts remain, OR include the drift report inline in the snapshot payload via a `Vec<(ProviderAccount, Option<DriftReport>)>` shape

F5-FIX-PROJECTED-P95-COLDSTART-1: Replace the n<10 seed `projected_tokens_p95 = cost_ceiling_tokens` with `projected_tokens_p95 = cost_ceiling_tokens.saturating_add(1)` — making the step 13.5 check fail-closed for cold-start; OR define a separate ColdStartPolicy::{Block,Allow} that the seed branch consults explicitly, so the no-op behavior is intentional and visible

F5-FIX-CHECKED-ADD-IN-PROJECTION-1: Replace `saturating_add` at v4 §B.4 step 7.5 with `checked_add` and propagate `None → SupervisorError::UsageBlocked('projected tokens overflow')`; add a unit test with `tokens_out = u64::MAX - 5` and `projected_p95 = 100`

F5-FIX-CAPABILITY-SEED-VALUE-VALIDATION-1: Replace v4 C.12.bis grep + v5 C.30 grep with a small TOML-parse gate (extension of `oya-dev-cli`) that asserts every driver row has `stop_hook_supported in {true, false}`, `request_id_supported in {true, false}`, `hooks_supported in {true, false}`, and `autonomy_tier in {T1Read,T2Suggest,T3PropAct,T4Actuate}` — not greps for substring presence

F5-FIX-WINDOWEXPIRED-LOCK-DISCIPLINE-1: Replace 'recurse once' at v4 §B.4 step 9 with explicit lock-release-then-iterate: release the step-1 lock, call rotate_window, return TickOutcome::Idle; let the next tick_once invocation re-peek-lock cleanly. No recursion, no implicit lock-stack

F5-FIX-AUTORECONCILE-RENDER-ERROR-PATH-1: Specify in v5 §B.4 the exact behavior when SettingsRenderer::render returns Err under VerifyMode::AutoReconcile — either propagate as SupervisorError variant OR exclude the account AND surface the error in the drift report; do not silently include

F5-FIX-DRIFT-DETECTION-STRUCTURAL-1: Extend SettingsRenderer::verify to support format-aware structural comparison for JSON and TOML targets (parse-then-AST-equality), keeping byte-blake3 only as a fast-path; emit DriftState::Modified only when the structural compare disagrees, not when bytes differ

F5-FIX-CODEX-OMITTED-HOOK-EVENTS-FIXTURE-GATE-1: Make Codex `omitted_hook_events = []` conditional on R1 fixture presence — if `crates/oya-foundry-settings-template-adapter-fs/tests/fixtures/codex-hooks.observed.json` is missing at scaffold, default Codex `omitted_hook_events` to the full HookEvent variant set and degrade Codex to no-op until the fixture lands
would_delete: Delete (a) the literal `.unwrap()` at v4 §B.4 step 5 and replace with `.ok_or(SupervisorError::NoEligibleAccount)?`; (b) the 'audit-only' claim on UsageWindowSnapshot — the snapshot's projected_tokens_p95 IS read for enforcement at step 13.5, so the audit-only label is false; (c) the n<10 seed `projected_tokens_p95 = cost_ceiling_tokens` — it makes the cost-ceiling check a no-op for every cold-start pair; (d) the C.12.bis + C.30 grep-based value gates — replace with a TOML-parse + enum-membership check; (e) the saturating_add at step 7.5 — replace with checked_add for hard cost ceilings; (f) the 'recurse once' on WindowExpired — replace with release-and-return-Idle so the lock discipline is explicit.
would_reshape: Reshape three places: (1) Move projected_tokens_p95 off UsageWindowSnapshot into a dedicated EnforcementProjection value that is plumbed separately to step 13.5 — the snapshot becomes truly audit-only; (2) Promote drift-induced account exclusion from a `.omc/state/settings-drift-report.json` side-channel to an explicit SupervisorError variant `AccountExcludedByDrift { account_id, drift_paths }` so the runtime cause is visible in the supervisor's own error path; (3) Specify the JsonlInbox dead_letter implementation strategy in an ADR (WAL or rename-journal) and add a crash-injection test that exercises the SIGKILL-between-release-and-write window — the trait-level 'atomic' doc-comment becomes a tested contract, not prose.
stage_coverage_note: Discovery-stage findings: surfaced ALL detected issues including LOW-severity and MEDIUM-confidence per F5 spec; ranking and filtering are downstream verification-stage concerns. Two CRITICAL HIGH-confidence findings (F5-CRIT-1 unwrap-in-library-code and F5-CRIT-2 enforcement-via-audit-field) would block APPROVE in a standalone code review; surfaced here for the consensus debate to weigh.
